about: EarthAtlas hand crosswalk: which IMO GISIS ISPS declared port facility (IMO Port Facility Number) is which terminal in salish-terminals.json. Reviewed 2026-09-27 from the GISIS 'Declared port facilities' CSV downloaded 2026-09-28 UTC (scripts/ships/gisis/raw/MaritimeSecurity-CheckOnlineForLatest-20260928-05155984.csv). decision 'link' = written as a terminal_links row (role imo_port_facility) when the import confirms the names share a main word AND the GISIS point lies within position_km of one of the terminal's berths, or the row carries a position_note explaining why GISIS's point is wrong. decision 'candidate' = names or roles do not clearly agree; never linked, kept here for review. Terminal names are not changed by this file. Used on Josh's instruction assuming IMO permission; written permission not yet obtained; the IMO Web Accounts policy otherwise forbids republishing. A row may also carry name_evidence (a sourced statement that two differently named entries are one facility); it stands in for the shared-word check, and is shown with the link.

rows.position_note: GISIS gives 48 25.20 N 123 22.25 W, a point in Victoria harbour (next to Port of Victoria CAVIC-0012), about 100 km from the Burnaby refinery: a GISIS data error. The name is used; the GISIS position is not.

rows.facility_name: Suncor Energy Products Partnership - Burrard Products Terminal

rows.note: GISIS lists G3 twice: CAVAC-0051 (port North Vancouver) and CAVAN-0081 (port Vancouver, description 'North Vancouver, BC'). Both are linked.

rows.position_note: GISIS gives 49 16.00 N 123 04.84 W, 2.3 km from the Alliance berth. The name is used; the GISIS position is not.

GISIS gives 49 17.29 N 123 06.38 W, the same longitude as Canada Place Cruise Terminal CAVAN-0003, about 5 km west of the Cascadia berth: a GISIS data error. The name is used; the GISIS position is not.

rows.note: GISIS lists Fraser Grain twice: CASUY-0002 (port Surrey, plan approved, updated 2026-05-25) and CAVAN-0079 (port Vancouver, plan not approved, last updated 2021-03-17). Both are linked.

rows.facility_name: Lehigh Hanson Materials Limited - Sechelt Pit
rows.position_note: GISIS gives 49 17.12 N 123 05.30 W, a point in Vancouver harbour about 50 km from Sechelt: a GISIS data error. GISIS also marks this facility's security plan withdrawn (2023-03-30). The name is used; the GISIS position is not.

rows.note: NOT the same facility (evidence 2026-09-28): Seaspan Energy runs its own LNG bunkering berth at Tilbury; LNG from FortisBC’s plant reaches Seaspan’s bunkering vessels “via trucks and ISO containers” until FortisBC’s Tilbury marine jetty is built (in service end of 2029): https://www.biv.com/news/resources-agriculture/lng-bunkering-fuels-3b-expansion-at-tilbury-island-12256257. Kept as a candidate; a separate Seaspan Energy terminal entry would be needed to show it.

Same facility. VAFFC’s own operations page names its new marine terminal “the South Fraser Marine Terminal” (“SFMT”): https://vancouverairportfuelfacility.ca/operations/ (read 2026-09-28). GISIS describes it as “Import of jet fuel from overseas”; the point is 0.22 km from the OSM berths.

rows.facility_name: PKM Canada Marine Terminal Limited Partnership
rows.note: Same facility: PKM Canada Marine Terminal LP is Pembina’s Vancouver Wharves company (Pembina page, 2026-09-28).
rows.name_evidence: Pembina’s Vancouver Wharves page names the operating company “PKM Canada Marine Terminal LP”: https://www.pembina.com/operations/facilities/vancouver-wharves/ (read 2026-09-28). The GISIS point is 0.37 km from the Vancouver Wharves berth.

rows.note: Same facility: DP World’s Nanaimo facility is the Duke Point terminal.
rows.name_evidence: DP World operates the Duke Point terminal in Nanaimo (https://www.dpworld.com/en/canada/projects/nanaimo, read 2026-09-28: “Duke Point Terminal”, 50-year lease with the Port of Nanaimo); the GISIS point is 0.78 km from the Duke Point berth, and no other DP World facility is near it.
